clue.text: Turn of Ruth numerically

definitions.note: the clue's adverb points to a position in numbered order, as with the number after third

indicators.note: a turn of something is a twist or rearrangement, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone checks which book of the Bible Ruth is, counting along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' rearranges the six letters of OF RUTH. Ruth is in fact the eighth book of the Bible, so the surface is only a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting one, two, three, four, the item in slot four takes this ordinal number.

clue.text: Robin's crime-fighting friend helpful to an Army officer

definitions.meaning: the caped superhero partnered by Robin in the comics
a soldier serving as an officer's personal servant in the British Army

explanation.surface: Robin's superhero partner turns out to be useful to a soldier too.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic-book hero shares his name with the British term for an officer's orderly or valet.

clue.text: Speechless over mislaying the script

definitions.meaning: unable to find anything to say
read literally: having lost the text, the actor is without the lines to speak

explanation.surface: An actor dries up on stage after losing the script.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: 'at a loss' is having mislaid something, and what is lost is the words, the script.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means struggling for anything to say, and taken literally it is having mislaid one's lines.

clue.text: Atone for being a one-time outright pirate

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-husband

indicators.note: split as 'out right': the letter R, short for right, goes out of the word before it

explanation.surface: A reformed buccaneer seeks forgiveness for his past life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outright' looks like an adjective meaning thorough, but read as 'R out' it removes R (right) from PIRATE, leaving PIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends or reparation for a wrong is to expiate it.

clue.text: Shy girl has flower that's drying up

parts.note: a person who dries up shrinks back, losing nerve; something shrinking is drying up and contracting
the violet is a small purple flower, also a girl's name

explanation.surface: A timid young woman owns a wilting bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: VIOLET does double service in the surface as both a girl's name and a flower; the full phrase is an idiom for a very shy person.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a timid, retiring person who avoids attention.

clue.text: By no means a small number saving goodbye to two quid

parts.note: No. is the short form of number, small because abbreviated
ta-ta is an informal British farewell

indicators.note: two signals that the letter for a pound is written twice

parts.note: a quid is a pound in British slang, and L (from libra) stands for pound

explanation.surface: A tiny sum is spared from two pounds being waved off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' joins the pieces. L is the pound sign's letter, from Latin libra, so two quid gives LL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are emphatic denials meaning in no way whatsoever.

clue.text: Italian composition for an Easter rendering

indicators.note: a rendering is a version or performance, so the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A piece of Italian music is played for the Easter service.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an Italian term for a serenade, a vocal or instrumental piece, often performed in the evening.

clue.text: Any rate, it isn't only charged to the nearest publican

definitions.meaning: a rate is a tax levied by a council in Britain

definitions.text: it isn't only charged to the nearest publican
definitions.meaning: read as a pun: the nearest pub is one's local, but this levy falls on everyone

explanation.surface: A remark that the council rate is levied on more people than the neighbourhood landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'local' is one's nearest pub, so the second reading plays on a publican running the local.
explanation.definitionFit: British rates were a council levy on property, the classic municipal charge.

clue.text: Bent on marriage?

definitions.meaning: slang for being caught or married, as a fish on a line

explanation.surface: Someone determined to get wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent on' looks like the idiom for determined; split, 'bent' is one definition and 'on marriage?' another, as in getting hitched.
explanation.definitionFit: Something curved like a hook is crooked, and a person caught in matrimony is said, informally, to be hitched or caught.

clue.text: Average for the golfer to knock back

indicators.note: knocking something back turns it round, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a rap is a sharp knock

explanation.surface: A typical golfer's score, enough to drink to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock back' looks like the idiom for downing a drink; 'back' reverses RAP, a knock.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the standard score for a hole is the expected number of strokes, so it is the norm or average.

clue.text: Famous clown anything but cheerful laid out

parts.note: grim means gloomy and stern

indicators.note: laid out suggests spread or set out anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrated joker lies flat, looking utterly miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LAID to ALDI. Joseph Grimaldi was the famous Regency clown of the London stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Grimaldi was the celebrated English pantomime performer whose name gave clowns the nickname Joey.

clue.text: She is followed by a victim of fratricide

parts.note: in Genesis Abel is killed by his brother Cain

explanation.surface: A woman is trailed by a murdered brother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followed by' puts the pieces in order. The definition 'She' is a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, a Spanish form of Elizabeth, so it can stand for any female.

clue.text: Orientals don't eat the food there, apparently

definitions.text: Orientals don't eat the food there, apparently

parts.words: Orientals don't eat the food there, apparently
parts.note: the food from this shop is taken home, so people from the East do not eat it on the premises

explanation.surface: A remark that people from the Far East never dine at a certain restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take away' is read literally: you do not eat the food there but carry it off.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese restaurant selling meals to carry out, so customers eat elsewhere.

clue.text: Local flower of Central Europe

definitions.meaning: a local is a pub, a public house near home
a river that flows through Switzerland, Austria and Germany

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood bloom from Central Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' here is a river, something that flows. The Inn is an Alpine river joining the Danube at Passau.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub or tavern serves as one's local, and the Inn is a river of Austria and Bavaria.

clue.text: Farewell party that maybe offends

indicators.note: maybe signals one possible arrangement of the following word's letters

explanation.surface: A leaving do that may upset people.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering to bid goodbye to someone departing.

clue.text: Yes, in a skating figure essential to see

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the figure that follows

parts.note: a figure of eight is traced on ice by skaters

explanation.surface: Yes, good vision matters when tracing figures on the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is the faculty one needs in order to see.

clue.text: Depressed area of a city?

parts.note: taken literally, a part of town that is down, low or sad, rather than the centre

explanation.surface: A rundown district of town.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: 'depressed' gives down and 'city' gives town, though the term means the central business district.
explanation.definitionFit: The city centre or business district, read as a downcast part of town.

clue.text: Relative to an impure condition

parts.note: an uncle is a family relation

explanation.surface: A family member brought into a dirty state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'condition' join the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritually or physically defiled, the opposite of pure.

clue.text: I object turning south for this Rhineland town

indicators.note: turning means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: the object form of I is me
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Someone objects to going south to a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' looks like a protest; it is grammar, the object form of I.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad Ems is a spa town on the river Lahn in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany.

clue.text: One for whom there's plenty in store

definitions.text: One for whom there's plenty in store

parts.words: One for whom there's plenty in store
parts.note: the phrase usually means a person with a bright future; literally it is someone in a shop with lots on the shelves

explanation.surface: A person with a lot to look forward to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plenty in store' is read literally: the store is a shop full of goods to buy.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer browsing goods in a shop.

clue.text: She should be Al at Lloyd's

definitions.text: She should be Al at Lloyd's

parts.words: She should be Al at Lloyd's
parts.note: a ship is called she, and A1 at Lloyd's is the top classification in Lloyd's Register of Shipping

explanation.surface: A woman ought to be top-rated by the insurers.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper prints A1 as 'Al'. Lloyd's Register rated ships, A1 meaning in first-class condition; ships are 'she'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship fit for the open sea earns the top rating in the shipping register.

clue.text: They may suit some drinkers, but not for long

definitions.meaning: small measures of spirits, preferred by some drinkers to long drinks
trousers cut above the knee, not long ones

explanation.surface: Some drinkers like these, though not for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' hides the clothing sense; 'not for long' means not long trousers, and long drinks are the opposite of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits served in small measures, and knee-length trousers, both share this name.

clue.text: Feeling against New York time change

indicators.note: change means the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Resentment over New York switching its time zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility, a sense of opposition towards someone.

clue.text: Orbits wildly into a restaurant

indicators.note: wildly means the letters are thrown about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something spins out of control into a café.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, informal eating house, French-style.

clue.text: Mother finally shows favour for such an account

parts.note: pro means in favour of
taken as written
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mum ends up supporting this kind of bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' sends MA to the end; 'shows' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro forma invoice is a preliminary bill sent in advance.

clue.text: Grave letters producing a tear

definitions.meaning: the abbreviation for rest in peace carved on headstones
to tear is to rend fabric

explanation.surface: An inscription on a tomb makes a mourner cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' looks like a teardrop; it is a rent in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Rest in peace is abbreviated on gravestones, and a rent in cloth is the same word.

clue.text: Bore witness to Sir Geoffrey being in South Dakota

indicators.note: being in means the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation of the US state
Sir Geoffrey Howe was a British Chancellor and Foreign Secretary under Thatcher

explanation.surface: A British statesman testifies while visiting the American Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Howe was a senior British Conservative minister in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonstrate or prove something is to bear witness to it.

clue.text: It's goodbye to paradise for mammals of the toothless order

parts.note: the Garden of Eden is the biblical paradise
ta-ta is an informal British farewell

explanation.surface: Animals without teeth bid farewell to their garden paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' and 'to' link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The scientific order of placental mammals with few or no teeth, such as anteaters and sloths.
